additional_info.subject: Further anlaysis
additional_info.body:
Upon analyzing the logs found that vehicle was charging fine on Jan 7th late evening, then interrupted by Err_Internal_comm error.
After this vehicle was still connected and tried restarting the charging session but abale to do that as it was getting failed at Authentication.
One thing I have noticed is that even the charging is not performing, Voltage Transducer at DC1 still detecting voltage around 400V to 600V.
I suspect that the vehicle contactors are welded that's why TF1 is detecting voltage.
Vehicle was connected till next morning which kept the outlet outoforder.
Err_Internal_comm
TF1 voltage while no charging

Dear Team,
We are reporting an issue with the Sicharge D charging station as the driver informed us that charging sessions are being interrupted unexpectedly. Two distinct interruptions were observed during the morning of January 9, 2025.
First Interruption

Following this interruption, the driver had to reconnect the vehicle to complete the charging session.
Second Interruption

Recurring Issue :
Based on feedback from drivers, a second Sicharge D station is experiencing similar issues. The serial number of the affected station is MP/R6 170002081.
Urgency and Recommendations :
This issue is particularly burdensome for operators and drivers, who need to constantly monitor the charging sessions. This is severely disrupting operations. Immediate intervention is required to address the situation.
Request for Local Intervention :
Please involve the local teams, particularly Sébastien and Franck, to enhance efficiency in diagnosing and resolving this issue. A permanent solution is essential to prevent these charging session interruptions from recurring.
At the present moment (10:54 AM, 09/01/2025), we observed a reduction in charging speed to 180 kW DC with a SoC between 54% and 56%. Could you please check if the power modules might be affected (See attached) ?
In addition
, I activated the DC3 connector and made it available. We disconnected the truck from the DC1 connector (the one on the left) and plugged it into the one on the right (DC3). Initially, we noticed a failure, and the station went into error mode (red indicator). The driver then unplugged and replugged the DC3 connector, and the charging session started correctly.
From this, I believe that the session ID was not created, which consequently caused the initial launch to fail.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0398322-DC/Si-D/FR-[4HIbKg]- Multiple chargers outlet out of order CRM:00645000918
additional_info.body:
Hi Malek,
Thank you for providing the detailed information.
We have done our first analysis of the logs from January 7th and 8th. Our findings indicate that the charging session was proceeding normally, delivering a current of approximately 200-300A. However, the session was suddenly interrupted due to a communication issue.
Subsequently, when the vehicle attempted to initiate a new charging session, it failed due to an authentication issue. The logs show that no authentication was performed. Additionally, the charger detected voltage at the output, which triggered insulation errors. We suspect there may have been issues from the vehicle side at that time.
Could you confirm if there were any incidents of the vehicle's output contactor being stuck? The charger's output contactors were open, yet voltage was detected at the output, which we suspect might have originated from the vehicle.
In the meantime, we will also analyze the logs for the timestamps you provided and share a detailed analysis soon.
Thank you
Best Regards,
Vishal Dhiman
eMobility Support Team

additional_info.subject: Re: ID0398322-DC/Si-D/FR-[4HIbKg]- Multiple chargers outlet out of order CRM:00645000918
additional_info.body:
Hello Vishal,
Where does the identification issue come from? I noticed that the session ID was not created. How and why did this happen? Is it related to the eCOG?
The same truck charges without any issues on a 160 kW Sicharge D station located right next to it and does not show these anomalies! I believe this hypothesis should be ruled out. Otherwise, how can we explain that it works on a 160 kW charger but not on a 300 kW one? Or did I receive a 300 kW charger that is obsolete and has technical problems?
Regarding these disconnection issues, the DC cable and CCS2 connector remain properly connected to the truck, which tries to establish communication, but the charger does not respond. This seems to be due to the lack of the Wake-Up BCB Toggle, making the Sicharge unable to restart a charging session. The driver had to reconnect his truck in the rain and cold 5 times today! Can you imagine yourself in his position? Is this normal?
A more detailed analysis must be conducted to identify the issues before blaming the truck, please. These same truck models work perfectly with other brands of chargers in our depots, without any issues.
Best regards,

Hi Malek,
We understand that repeatedly restarting the session can be inconvenient in this situation.
Based on our initial analysis, we observed this behavior and suspected it might indicate an issue. Our intention was not to assign blame but to be transparent and confirm the observations from your side as well.
